text:
juno: Quick PSA — I ran the new example in the API reference for POST /v1/uploads against local dev and got a 415. The docs show a JSON payload (`{ \"url\": \"https://...\" }`) and a sample curl using `-d`, but the runtime only accepts multipart form for file bytes. I opened a tiny PR to swap the main example to multipart and add a note about URL-only JSON. PR: #3301

ravi: saw the 415 too when smoke-testing. The error in the server logs is `Unsupported Media Type: expected multipart/form-data`. So definitely docs -> runtime mismatch.

docs-bot: PR #3301 by juno: docs: switch uploads main example to multipart/form-data, add FormData TS snippet, add OpenAPI content-type. (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3301) :page_with_curl:

anya: Good catch. To be explicit in the reference, can we show: 1) curl multipart sample for binary files, 2) fetch/TS FormData snippet, 3) small JSON example for the "remote URL" flow (the service will fetch the URL).

juno: yep — here's the curl I'm proposing: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\n  -F "file=@./photo.jpg" \\n  -F "purpose=semantic_search"
```
Note: we explicitly call out that `-F` creates multipart/form-data.

ravi: for the JSON-only case maybe show this small example and note it's only for remote fetches: ```json
{ "url": "https://example.com/large.pdf", "purpose": "document_ingest" }
```
And a sentence: "Do not use JSON for binary file uploads; binary must be multipart/form-data."

keith: On the OpenAPI side: current spec only declares `application/json`. I'll add `multipart/form-data` under `requestBody.content` with schema: `type: object`, properties: `file` (type: string, format: binary), `purpose` (type: string, enum: ["semantic_search","vector_index","document_ingest"]) and also keep `application/json` for the remote-url shape. I'll run `openapi-cli validate` after the patch.

anya: For the fetch snippet use this variant (browser-safe): ```ts
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fileInput.files[0]);
form.append('purpose', 'semantic_search');
const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}` },
  body: form,
});
const body = await resp.json();
console.log('upload_ref:', body.upload_ref, 'name:', body.filename);
```
Add note: "Do not set Content-Type header manually when using FormData in browsers; the browser will add the correct boundary."

juno: small twist — the runtime changed the response shape in the last deploy. Instead of `file_id` it now returns `upload_ref` and `filename`. I'll add a migration blurb at the top of the docs page: `2026-03-23: response field renamed file_id -> upload_ref; update client code.`

docs-bot: checklist update for PR #3301: snippets added, openapi pending (keith), migration note added (juno), docs smoke-tests pending (ravi).

ravi: I'll add a quick smoke test to `docs/test/acceptance/upload-samples.md`: step 1 run the curl against local dev; step 2 assert 2xx and `upload_ref` in JSON. That should catch regressions if somebody accidentally reverts to JSON-only examples.

keith: updating OpenAPI now. One gotcha: swagger-ui will try to render `file` as `binary` — make sure the examples show `file: <choose a file>` and the UI example still allows demonstrating the JSON remote-url shape. I'll run the docs build locally and verify the example blocks render correctly.

juno: thanks all. After merge I'll open a tiny follow-up to add a note in the SDK migration guide (docs/sdk/migration.md): `replace file_id with upload_ref for the uploads endpoint` and add a minimal unit test snippet in the Python SDK examples to read `upload_ref` from the response.

anya: also add a short "why" line: we moved to a content-addressed blob store and the stable ref is now `upload_ref` (not an incremental numeric id) so SDKs should treat it as an opaque string.

keith: CI failing on schema lint — I fixed one indentation issue and re-ran. Should be green in ~5m.

docs-bot: PR #3301 CI: running -> green (docs build + linkcheck + openapi-lint).

ravi: merged and closed. I also ran the acceptance step locally and it passed.

juno: merged — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the SDK note.
